_comment: GENERATED by `python3 -m edge_workbench check`. Do not edit:
re-run it. This is what the build reads instead of the
tutorial, so that a build depends on files in this repository
and not on which branch a sibling checkout happens to be on.
`source.sha` is the commit the tutorial was read at. A gate
compares it against the tutorial's head to tell you when the
tutorial has moved and this needs re-running.
`gaps` lists what the tutorial does not state in a form this
step can read. Those are the model-assisted half's input; an
empty list means the tutorial said everything itself.

example.quote: Take the five-vertex graph with unit edges

meanings.init: The search starts with only the sources on the frontier, at depth 0, already marked visited.

tensorNotes.G: the graph: an entry of 1 is an edge s to d
tensorNotes.F: the frontier: the depth of each vertex discovered in this generation
tensorNotes.T: candidate depths one hop beyond the frontier
tensorNotes.P: the visited mask: True once a vertex has been reached

E01.graph: Every vertex on the frontier offers each out-neighbour a depth one more than its own.
E01.einsum: For each destination $d$, add $G_{s,d}$ to $F_{i,s}$ wherever both are present, then reduce over $s$, keeping any one of the equal sums.

E02.graph: Keep a candidate depth only for vertices not yet visited; they form the next frontier.
E02.einsum: Take $T_{i,d}$ exactly where $\neg P_{i,d}$ is present, that is, where $P_{i,d}$ is empty.

E03.graph: Mark the vertices of the new frontier as visited, keeping the earlier marks.
E03.einsum: OR $P_{i,d}$ with $F_{i+1,d}$ over $d$, wherever either is present.

stop.graph: Stop when no vertex was newly discovered.
stop.einsum: Halt when the occupancy of $F_{i+1}$, its count of non-empty entries, is zero.

quotes.init: Initialization places the source at depth $0$ and marks it visited:
